properties.name: The MCP server keeps working as it is for the people who use it, and what is improved for the --call door is additive or opt-in
properties.source: Anthony (who:ajs), 2026-10-05, relayed verbatim to this session by the dev_reflow2 hub session
properties.statement:
A person who uses reflow2 as an MCP server, the way it was originally designed, shall keep getting the server they use today when reflow2 is improved for the `--call` door (an agent such as VS Code's Copilot where MCP is blocked). An improvement made for the door is ADDITIVE (a new tool, a new field or a new line in a reply; never an existing tool, field or reply shape renamed, removed or given a new meaning) or it is OPT-IN, behind a flag or setting the door's user turns on. Where both can be supported, both are.

IN ANTHONY'S WORDS, 2026-10-05: "I just want to make sure the changes we implement for vscode don't break it for how it was originally used/designed as an mcp server. My brother likes using as is, so I don't want to break it for him by introducing changes to make it work better for vscode --call option. If it can support both, that's great. And when I run it with vscode at work, maybe I configure it with "reflow2 --use-call" or some other flags that make it work for vscode call".

ENFORCEMENT, RECOMMENDED AND NOT YET APPROVED: a CI gate that pins the existing tools' schemas and reply shapes. The input schemas are already pinned (tools/toolsnap.py against the goldens in tools/toolsnaps/). Reply shapes are not pinned by anything. Building that half is Anthony's call and has not been made.

SIBLING of req:reflow2-keeps-working-entirely-on-one-machine (accepted 2026-09-25), which keeps the local, sign-in-free setup; this one keeps the MCP surface its current users rely on while the door improves. Searched first: no existing requirement covered backwards compatibility of the served surface.

AMENDED on @ajs's word, 2026-10-13, ruling on the judgement pass ("Go with your recommendations"). He first leaned toward retiring this requirement, because "only ever add" blocks every via-negativa cut. The recommendation he took was to amend it rather than retire it.

WHAT STAYS: a person using the MCP server as originally designed keeps getting the server they use today. Door improvements stay additive or opt-in.

WHAT CHANGES: "never removed" becomes "never removed WITHOUT A RELEASE OF NOTICE". Anything a client can call or read (a tool, a field, a node type, a reply shape) is retired in two releases:
(1) A DEPRECATING release, in which it still works, says it is going (in its tool description, or in describe_schema for a schema item), and the changelog carries a "What to do" line. Alex hears before it ships.
(2) The NEXT release removes it.
This is the same discipline the accepted tool rule already applies to tools (dec:a-tool-is-never-deleted-without-usage-evidence-across-projects-and-never-without-a-refusing-stub-first), extended to every served item.

The check that the served surface only grows becomes a check that it shrinks only through a deprecating release. This is the retirement rule dec:anchor-retire-or-implement waits on. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
